# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## mercury
Mercury coordination substrate: typed tools for file leases, the crew brief (the same live read LiveComms gives), and crew messaging. Prefer these over Bash for swarm coordination.
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- update-config: Use this skill for any change to Mercury settings files: permission rules ("allow X"), environment variables ("set X=Y"), MCP server enablement, extension settings, and every event-driven automation ("whenever X, do Y" — that is a hook, and only a h…
- keybindings-help: Use when the user asks to change Mercury keyboard shortcuts: rebind an action, add a chord sequence, bind a slash command to a key, unbind a default, or fix keybinding errors reported by /health. Carries the file layers, the keystroke grammar, and t…
- simplify: Use when the user asks to clean up, simplify, or tighten changed code: a quality-only pass over the working diff for reuse, shape, and cost improvements, applied directly. It does not hunt for bugs — adversarial checking is /verify.
- app-proof: Use when proving a web journey with Mercury's Browser and Service tools. Not for unit tests.
- extension-maker: Use when building or repairing a Mercury extension or catalogue. Not for installing or approving one for the operator.
- mcp-smithy: Use when building an MCP server for a Mercury session and proving its tool contract. Not for configuring an existing server.
- pdf-documents: Use when inspecting, creating or changing PDFs, including forms and redaction. Not for editing an Office source document.
- provider-apis: Use when building against model-provider APIs or choosing request shapes, streaming, tools or caching for Mercury's providers. Not for account sign-in or unrelated SDKs.
- skill-forge: Use when writing or fixing a Mercury SKILL.md and its discovery rules. Not for /skillify session capture or extension packaging.
- slide-decks: Use when creating or revising PowerPoint slides, layouts and notes. Not for web interfaces or prose documents.
- spreadsheets: Use when editing Excel workbooks or turning tabular data into one without losing formulas. Not for databases or other Office files.
- word-documents: Use when creating or revising a Word file while preserving its document structure. Not for plain-text drafting or PDF editing.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command repeatedly (for example /loop 10m /health); with no interval given, the model paces itself between ticks. - Use when work should re-run on a cadence: polling a build, watching a queue, periodic upkeep. A single future r…
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled local agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule via the daemon - Use when the user wants a recurring agent, automated background tasks, a cron job for the harness, or management of existing scheduled ag…
- deep-research: Multi-source research with adversarial fact-checking — angle fan-out, source extraction, majority-vote verification, cited synthesis. - For research that needs many sources and real fact-checking. Scale with honesty: full depth runs roughly 25-40 ag…
</system-reminder>
